2847d66d5679ee28e006b3eb2a330eebdd20bdcb.summary: Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group report zero-day exploitation of CVE-2026-22769 in Dell RecoverPoint for Virtual Machines by UNC6201, a suspected PRC-nexus threat cluster, active since at least mid-2024. The actor deployed SLAYSTYLE, BRICKSTORM and the new GRIMBOLT backdoor, and pivoted into VMware infrastructure using Ghost NICs and iptables-based single packet authorization. Dell has released remediations.

28ca30af74645877c18b6ca1c60a9c8873987815.summary: 360 Advanced Threat Research Institute reports a campaign by APT-C-28 (also called ScarCruft or APT37), linked to North Korea. Phishing emails carry LNK files that start PowerShell and load the RokRat remote access tool in memory. Targets are government personnel and corporations in South Korea and Asia. The 2024 RokRat variant adds anti-forensic cleanup and process hollowing. The report advises email filtering, PowerShell monitoring and application allowlisting.

28daf3ac0fd51cfb17d851fe8469d7f8a620452b.summary: French-language threat report (TLP:WHITE, created 22/10/2019, published 23/04/2020) on Silence, a cybercrime group described as allegedly Russian-speaking and active since 2016, targeting banks and ATM networks. It describes phishing with malicious attachments, the Truebot downloader, an Atmosphere DLL injected into ATM management software, compromise of card-processing systems via stolen employee credentials, and cash-outs by money mules. Cited thefts total about 4.2 million dollars from 2016 to 2019. The report suggests possible links to TA505, which it hedges as possibly stemming from…

hedges: Silence is described as allegedly Russian-speaking and independent (supposément russophones et indépendants).
Per Group-IB, French IP addresses 'would have' communicated with Silence's C2 infrastructure in 2019.
The agency says it is unaware of France being targeted, but it is not excluded that France may be or have been targeted.
The roughly 4.2 million dollars stolen from banks is stated with 'aurait' (would have).
Links between Silence and TA505 are described as possibly due to Silence buying bank network access ('il se pourrait').
The report says a Lazarus technique 'would' use malicious code to approve fraudulent ATM withdrawals.
Lack of PCI DSS compliance is said to facilitate attacks ('seraient facilitées'), an explanation the report hedges.
The ATM DLL-injection technique is said to predate Silence, citing open-source material from 2009.
